claims.title: Flooding sign-in requests can exhaust the central identity broker
claims.description: An external attacker can send high-rate sign-in attempts over the boundary-crossing `flow:colleague-to-identity-broker:sign-in` to the internet-facing `process:identity-broker`. If request admission, credential processing, request-size limits, and rate/cost controls are not enforced before sign-in work, each cheap attempt can consume broker worker CPU and connection capacity while the broker reads `store:directory`, accesses `store:key-store` to issue tokens, and writes sign-in activity to `store:audit-log`. The flow's `authentication` is unknown, so it is unverified whether unauthenticated or malformed attempts are rejected before this work. Second-order, exhausting the broker prevents legitimate colleagues from obtaining tokens and can also block `process:store-admin-console` from fetching signing material over `flow:store-admin-console-to-identity-broker:fetch-public-key`; as the central sign-in service, its outage affects applications relying on broker-issued tokens.

grounds.text: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:colleague-to-identity-broker:sign-in`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditionally on the unverified request-authentication and load-control posture: `process:identity-broker` is internet-facing and `flow:colleague-to-identity-broker:sign-in` crosses from `boundary:outside-corporate-network`, allowing remote attackers to repeatedly attempt sign-in work. Impact is high because `process:identity-broker` is tagged `availability-critical` and is the shared issuer for colleague tokens, while `process:store-admin-console` also depends on it through `flow:store-admin-console-to-identity-broker:fetch-public-key`.

mitigations.summary: Apply pre-authentication rate and cost limits to sign-in traffic
mitigations.detail: Enforce per-source and, after identification, per-account rate limits and concurrency budgets on `flow:colleague-to-identity-broker:sign-in`; reject oversized or malformed requests before credential validation, directory access, token signing, or audit writes.

mitigations.summary: Bound broker dependency use and shed excess work
mitigations.detail: Use short read and idle timeouts, bounded worker and connection pools, and fail-fast load shedding for `process:identity-broker` access to `store:directory`, `store:key-store`, and `store:audit-log` so a request flood cannot queue indefinitely.

mitigations.summary: Protect relying applications from broker stalls
mitigations.detail: Set timeouts and circuit breakers on `flow:store-admin-console-to-identity-broker:fetch-public-key`, and use safely cached, rotated public signing keys where appropriate so a temporary broker overload does not immediately prevent token validation.

claims.title: Store-manager tokens authorize financial changes at every store
claims.description: An authenticated colleague who legitimately holds a store-manager token can use `flow:colleague-to-store-admin-console:change-prices-and-void` to command `process:store-admin-console` to change prices or void transactions for stores other than their own. The console uses the group claim but does not bind the requested store to the token holder's assigned store, so this is horizontal authorization escalation rather than identity impersonation. The terminal capability is financial and business-data alteration across every store served by the console.

grounds.text: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high because any authenticated store manager can submit an ordinary request over `flow:colleague-to-store-admin-console:change-prices-and-void`, which crosses into the corporate network, without needing to bypass authentication. Impact is high because the flow permits price changes and transaction voids against any store and is tagged `financial` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Enforce store-level authorization on every console operation
mitigations.detail: Have `process:store-admin-console` derive the colleague and permitted store scope from the verified token, then deny price-change and void requests whose target store is outside that scope.

mitigations.summary: Constrain administrative tokens to explicit store scopes
mitigations.detail: Include an authoritative store assignment or scoped role in broker-issued tokens and validate it server-side rather than relying on the broad store-manager group alone.

claims.title: Remote sign-in credentials and bearer tokens may be intercepted in transit

Its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If transport encryption is not enforced end-to-end, an attacker able to observe the colleague's remote network path can intercept credentials and the returned bearer token. The token can then be presented to relying applications such as `process:store-admin-console`; its group claims govern access without a callback to the broker, extending the disclosure into unauthorized use of the colleague's application access.

Second-order, a token for an identity with the store-manager group can be presented to `process:store-admin-console`, whose authorization is based on token groups and works against every store. mitigations.summary: Require signed and authenticated federation assertions

mitigations.detail: Define which franchise identities may be vouched for and ensure federation assertions cannot map to arbitrary internal privileged identities or groups.

claims.title: Unbounded franchise federation may grant corporate sign-in authority beyond the partner's approved population
claims.description: A party controlling `entity:franchise-identity-provider` can use `flow:franchise-identity-provider-to-identity-broker:vouch-for-colleague` to ask `process:identity-broker` to treat an asserted franchise colleague as signed in. That flow leaves the tenant boundary `boundary:franchise-partner` and enters the corporate network, but the authorized population the provider may vouch for is not documented. If the broker does not enforce a per-request federation scope, the partner can use its legitimate provider authority to obtain broker-issued tokens for individuals outside the intended franchise population. Those tokens are accepted by relying applications according to their group claims, extending the partner's authority into corporate application access.

grounds.text: We have not written down which colleagues that provider is allowed to vouch for.
Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.

verdict.reason: The model says the permitted population for franchise assertions is not written down, but does not establish whether the broker enforces a per-request federation scope; the asserted authorization escalation is therefore conditional on that unresolved control.

related_unknowns.subject: Does the identity broker enforce a per-request federation scope that limits the franchise identity provider to its approved population?

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unstated federation-scope enforcement: the attacker must control or misuse the franchise provider, but can then submit assertions on the boundary-crossing federation flow. Impact is medium because success obtains corporate broker-issued application access, while the model does not establish which group mappings or application privileges franchise assertions receive.

mitigations.summary: Enforce an explicit federation authorization policy at the broker
mitigations.detail: Require `process:identity-broker` to validate issuer, audience, subject namespace, and an allowlisted franchise population for every assertion on `flow:franchise-identity-provider-to-identity-broker:vouch-for-colleague`.

mitigations.summary: Constrain franchise-issued application authority
mitigations.detail: Map franchise identities only to narrowly scoped franchise roles and deny corporate administrative groups by default; re-evaluate the partner authorization on every sign-in rather than treating the assertion alone as sufficient.

claims.title: A storage-layer copy of the directory may expose colleague identities and group memberships
claims.description: `store:directory` contains colleague records and group memberships used by `process:identity-broker`, but both its data classification and `encryption_at_rest` are unknown. If the unverified at-rest control resolves to unencrypted storage, a person who obtains a disk, snapshot, backup, or other operational copy can read the directory directly without authenticating through the broker. The resulting PII and group mapping can be used to target named colleagues and identify privileged groups for later attacks against `flow:colleague-to-identity-broker:sign-in` and relying applications. This is conditional on encryption at rest being absent or ineffective.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the directory and every operational copy

mitigations.summary: Minimize and restrict directory copies
mitigations.detail: Limit backup/export access to dedicated principals, retain only necessary directory fields, and monitor export or snapshot operations involving colleague and group data.

claims.title: Unscoped franchise assertions can create unauthorized federated identities
claims.description: `flow:franchise-identity-provider-to-identity-broker:vouch-for-colleague` crosses the tenant boundary from `boundary:franchise-partner` into `boundary:corporate-network`, and `process:identity-broker` accepts the franchise provider's assertion as a sign-in while the permitted colleague population is not written down. If the broker does not validate a tenant-scoped subject policy, a franchise party able to issue assertions can impersonate identities beyond the franchise colleagues it should represent and obtain broker-issued tokens. Second-order: applications including `process:store-admin-console` make decisions from broker token groups, so an improperly federated identity can become an application identity; the exact assertion validation and permitted-subject policy must be established.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium, conditional on absent or ineffective subject-scope enforcement, because exploitation requires control or misuse of the separate franchise provider on `flow:franchise-identity-provider-to-identity-broker:vouch-for-colleague`. Impact is medium because the model establishes that relying applications use broker token group claims, but does not establish what groups or application privileges an out-of-scope franchise assertion receives.

mitigations.summary: Enforce tenant-scoped federation policy at the broker
mitigations.detail: Require `process:identity-broker` to validate issuer, signature, audience, expiry, and a configured allowlist or claim policy binding `entity:franchise-identity-provider` to only its authorized franchise subjects.

mitigations.summary: Bind downstream authorization to verified tenant and store claims
mitigations.detail: Include a verified franchise/store scope in broker-issued tokens and make `process:store-admin-console` enforce that scope rather than relying on a store-manager group alone.

claims.title: Unverified directory write authentication could permit group-membership tampering
claims.description: `flow:identity-broker-to-directory:read-write-directory` has `authentication: unknown` while it performs read-write operations against `store:directory`. If that unknown resolves to missing or overly broad write authorization, an attacker who gains reach to the corporate-network store interface can alter colleague records or group memberships directly. `process:identity-broker` reads the directory at sign-in and uses its group data to issue tokens; the altered membership therefore becomes authorization input for every relying application, including `process:store-admin-console` and its financial write operations. This is conditional on the unverified caller authentication and authorization model.

grounds.text: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:identity-broker-to-directory:read-write-directory`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional on unknown authentication because the directory is inside `boundary:corporate-network`, so the attacker needs a corporate-network foothold in addition to an unprotected or over-privileged write path. Impact is high because changing group memberships in `store:directory` affects tokens issued by `process:identity-broker` and can authorize financial changes through `process:store-admin-console`.

mitigations.summary: Establish least-privilege directory write authentication
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated workload identity for `process:identity-broker` on `flow:identity-broker-to-directory:read-write-directory`, deny all other writers by default, and limit it to required directory operations.

mitigations.summary: Protect privileged group changes
mitigations.detail: Require server-side authorization, versioned changes, and independent alerts or approval for modifications to groups that grant administrative or financial capabilities.

rejected_claims.title: A departed manager can retain administrative authority until token expiry
rejected_claims.description: A colleague who was legitimately issued a store-manager token can retain and use it on `flow:colleague-to-store-admin-console:change-prices-and-void` after their HR removal, because `process:store-admin-console` does not re-check with `process:identity-broker` and issued tokens cannot be withdrawn before their twelve-hour expiry. The former colleague therefore continues to exercise authority no longer legitimately granted; combined with the console's unrestricted store targeting, the retained authority reaches price and transaction controls for every store.

grounds.text: The broker pulls the changes once a night, and that is also how leavers stop being colleagues. Tokens are good for twelve hours and there is no way to pull one back before it expires.

Impact is high because that token can reach `process:store-admin-console` operations tagged `financial` and `business-critical-data`, including changes and voids against any store.

mitigations.summary: Make authorization changes effective immediately
mitigations.detail: Use short-lived tokens with an active-session or token-revocation check at `process:store-admin-console`, so HR-driven removal invalidates administrative access before the existing token expires.

mitigations.summary: Publish timely deprovisioning signals from HR
mitigations.detail: Replace the nightly-only group update with prompt revocation or event-driven group removal to reduce the period in which the broker can validate departed staff.

rejected_claims.title: Compromise of the internet-facing broker yields universal token-signing authority
rejected_claims.description: An attacker who obtains control of internet-facing `process:identity-broker` inherits its ability to read the signing secret through `flow:identity-broker-to-key-store:read-signing-key` from `store:key-store`. The attacker can then mint tokens that validate wherever the shared signing key is trusted, thereby gaining the authority of token holders at relying applications rather than merely access to the broker. Second-order, because one key signs tokens for every application, the terminal capability is cross-application authorization escalation, including any application that grants administrative actions from token group claims.

grounds.text: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because `process:identity-broker` is reachable through the boundary-crossing `flow:colleague-to-identity-broker:sign-in`, but this chain still requires compromise of that process. Impact is high because `store:key-store` holds a secret used to sign tokens for every application, creating cross-application authority.

mitigations.summary: Isolate signing authority from the internet-facing broker
mitigations.detail: Move key use behind a tightly authorized signing service or hardware-backed key boundary, so compromise of `process:identity-broker` does not expose reusable token-signing material.

mitigations.summary: Limit the blast radius of issuer credentials
mitigations.detail: Use separate keys and strict audience validation for distinct relying applications, rotate keys regularly, and ensure applications reject tokens not explicitly minted for their audience.
